newsitem.title: KENYA: SAB TO BUILD $45 MLN BREWERY IN KENYA.
newsitem.headline: SAB TO BUILD $45 MLN BREWERY IN KENYA.

text.p: South African Breweries Limited (SAB) plans to build a $45 million brewery in Kenya, the company said on Thursday.
According to a statement released through the South African High Commission in Kenya, the brewery will have a capacity of 800,000 hectolitres per year and is expected to create 700 jobs.

"We believe current beer consumption levels in Kenya are less than half what they should be,'' said Andre Parker, managing director of SAB's international division. "There exists room for growth in the market through healthy competition.
The brewery, to built at Thika on the outskirts of Nairobi, will be owned jointly by Donyo Sabuk Holdings -- a consortium of Kenyan entrepreneurs; Dutch development agency DMO; and SAB.
It is scheduled to be fully operational at the end of next year and will seek a Nairobi Stock Exchange listing once established.
